value.rules_markdown:
- Use rustfmt output, Rust 2024 idioms; snake_case for modules/files, PascalCase for types.
- Return Result<T> using the crate error type from src/error.rs.
- Every file opens with a //! module doc describing role and feature gating.
- Comments explain the decision, not the code; note load-bearing flags/ordering.
- Public items have doc comments; Clap fields use /// for help text.
- Place tests in-crate in #[cfg(test)] mod tests; move to sibling test.rs when large; no tests/ directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock; MockForge records writes for assertions.
- Cover lane behavior with golden tests: fixture diff + canned model response, assert filtered/deduped/capped findings.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behavior.
- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split and link when exceeded.
- Model never holds write token; lanes run read-only; write credentials minted only in src/apply after all model calls.
- Contributor code is never executed; only read diff/tree, no build/install/run scripts.
- Treat PR bodies, comments, diffs as untrusted input; label as data in prompts; model verdict advisory, only deterministic policy in src/apply/automerge may mutate.
- Report secrets by type and location only; never include value in comment, check-run, or log.
- Use concise imperative commit subjects; keep commits small; commit each coherent validated slice.
- PRs state what changed, any behavior change, and how verified.
- One responsibility per module; core types in module-local types.rs; each port in src/ports/ is one trait/file.
- Declare every subcommand in src/bin/tinysweeper.rs even if unimplemented.
- Presets are data not code; adding a preset is a new folder, never a new module.
- Never edit vendor/tinyagents directly; change upstream and bump pin.
- Write one docs/modules/<module>/README.md per src module.
- Declare examples in Cargo.toml with required-features.
- Default build is offline; network access behind features (harness, github, serve).
